title: The Mirror Maze
story: You and NOVA are in a hall of mirrors, testing NOVA's robot camera, when the exit locks. Computers 'see' with cameras, a little like eyes. Help NOVA understand light to find the way out.
escaped: The exit appears in the mirrors. NOVA now sorts surfaces by how they reflect, follows the laws of reflection and learns from how eyes work.

locks.title: Clear reflection or not?
locks.intro: NOVA's camera must sort surfaces into those giving regular reflection (a clear image) and diffused reflection. Choose its clues.
locks.hint: Marble is white like paper; rusty iron is a metal like the spoon. What makes reflection clear?
locks.learn: Colour and material fooled NOVA's camera. Regular reflection depends on the surface being smooth, so that is the clue a machine should use.

locks.title: Check NOVA's mirror maths
locks.intro: NOVA is aiming a laser at a mirror. Is its claim right? Decide and pick the fact that settles it.
locks.claim: Light hitting a mirror at an angle of 30° bounces off at 60°.
evidence: The angle of reflection is always equal to the angle of incidence.
A mirror image is swapped left to right.
White light is made of seven colours.
The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in one plane.
locks.hint: Which law of reflection is about angles?
locks.learn: Two of these are real laws of reflection, but only one tests NOVA's number. Good checking picks the evidence that matches the exact claim.

locks.title: Learn from the eye
locks.intro: NOVA studied how the pupil of the human eye changes with light, to copy it for its camera opening.
locks.question: NOVA's camera is going into a dim cinema hall. Following the eye's pattern, what should it do?
options: Open its opening wider to let in more light.
Keep it the same size; light doesn't matter.
locks.hint: In the table, what happens to the pupil as it gets darker?
locks.learn: Engineers copy patterns from nature. The iris makes the pupil bigger in dim light to let more light in, and cameras do the same.

locks.title: Fix NOVA's eye diagram
locks.intro: NOVA has labelled parts of the eye. Tick the labels that are wrong.

rows.label: Clear front part of the eye
Controls the size of the pupil
Sense colour
rows.why: rods respond to dim light; cones sense colour

rows.label: Gives the eye its colour
rows.why: the iris gives the eye its colour

locks.hint: Rods and cones are two kinds of cells. Which part is coloured?
locks.learn: A machine that learned from these labels would 'know' the wrong things about vision. Checking labels matters even for diagrams.
